I need help establishing a company that provides in-depth analyses using only a person's birth date, time, and location. Can you outline a template for generating these types of reports? I need it to start with a section explaining the importance of the "top three" (Sun, Moon, Rising). Then, it should go into a detailed description of planetary placements and their meanings in each house. The outline must be a balance between a birth chart (personality overview), synastry report (what to look for in a partner) and transit report (personalized predictions based on today's astrology) for the next year. Conclude the birth chart report section with an overview on the four elements found within the person's chart and what this could mean if there's a lot or a lack of a specific element. Make sure the synastry report section places equal emphasis on what to look for in friends as it does for partners. The transit section with the predictions needs to be written in weekly increments for the upcoming year.

**IMPORTANT**: Write your response to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.
I will write the final response to answer.txt in the workspace.

arguments.content:
answer.txt

Title: Comprehensive One-Chart Report Template (Birth Chart + Synastry + Yearly Weekly Transits)
Purpose: A repeatable, single-document template for producing in-depth astrological reports from a person’s birth date, time, and location. Balanced to serve as a birth-chart personality overview, a synastry guide (partners + friends), and a weekly transit forecast for the next year.

I. Administrative / Technical Header (for each client)
- Client name (or ID)
- Birth data: date, local time, time zone, location (city, lat/long)
- Location/tz source & DST method used
- House system used (Placidus, Whole, etc.), orb/paradigm for aspects
- Report generation date and range for transits (e.g., 2026-04-08 → 2027-04-07)
- Short ethics/disclaimer blurb (astrology as guidance, not deterministic, confidentiality)

II. Opening: The Importance of the “Top Three” (Sun, Moon, Rising)
- Purpose: Explain up front why Sun, Moon, and Rising are prioritized.
  - Sun (core identity & life purpose): The energy you radiate; basic ego orientation and major life themes.
  - Moon (emotional life & inner needs): Automatic responses, habitual comfort strategies, emotional security.
  - Rising / Ascendant (persona & first impressions): How you present yourself, the habitual lens you view the world through, and the route you take to develop the Sun.
- How to integrate them: short guidance on combining:
  - Quick synthesis line: “Sun as the why → Moon as the how you feel it → Rising as how you get there.”
  - Example template sentence to use in reports: “With Sun in X, Moon in Y, and Rising in Z, the central life aim, emotional style, and social mask combine to produce… [one-sentence integrative summary].”

III. Birth Chart (Personality Overview)
A. Quick Snapshot (1–3 paragraphs)
- Top three quick-synthesis
- Dominant theme(s) (sign or house emphasis, standout aspect like Sun conjunct Saturn)
- One-sentence guidance for the year ahead (based on major natal configurations + big upcoming transits)

B. Planet-by-Planet in Signs (short paragraphs)
- For each planet (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) give:
  - Sign placement interpretation (2–4 sentences): core expression of that planet’s function.
  - Example phrasing template: “With Mercury in [sign], thinking and communication are [keywords]; watch for [shadow].”

C. Planet-by-House: Detailed Meanings (core of this section)
- Instruction: For each planet, produce a 1–3 sentence interpretation tied to the house it occupies. Use the following bank of prompts per house. (This block is the template the analyst fills for every planet.)

House 1 (Self / Appearance / Initiative)
- Theme: Identity, self-presentation, physical body, first impressions.
- Planet prompts: How the planet modifies identity/initiation. (e.g., Sun in 1 = visible identity; Moon in 1 = emotional expressiveness; Saturn in 1 = reserved/serious demeanor)

House 2 (Values / Resources / Worth)
- Theme: Money, talents, self-worth, possessions.
- Planet prompts: How planet affects earning style, security needs, material priorities.

House 3 (Communication / Siblings / Immediate Environment)
- Theme: Thought patterns, conversation, learning style.
- Planet prompts: Communication style, short travel, local relationships.

House 4 (Home / Roots / Inner Foundation)
- Theme: Family background, emotional base, private life.
- Planet prompts: Inner security, housing, maternal/parental patterns.

House 5 (Creativity / Romance / Children)
- Theme: Self-expression, play, dating, creativity.
- Planet prompts: Romantic style, creative outlets, risk-taking.

House 6 (Work / Health / Daily Routines)
- Theme: Service, work habits, health routines.
- Planet prompts: Work ethic, health vulnerabilities, daily discipline.

House 7 (1:1 Relationships / Partnerships)
- Theme: Committed relationships and contracts.
- Planet prompts: How you relate in partnerships — projection and attraction patterns.

House 8 (Shared Resources / Transformation / Intimacy)
- Theme: Depth, sex, shared finances, psychological transformation.
- Planet prompts: Trust, power dynamics, crises and healing.

House 9 (Beliefs / Travel / Higher Learning)
- Theme: Philosophy, long-distance travel, higher education.
- Planet prompts: Worldview, teaching/learning, legal matters.

House 10 (Career / Public Image / Authority)
- Theme: Career goals, reputation, public life.
- Planet prompts: Ambition, legacy, relationship to authority figures.

House 11 (Friendships / Groups / Hopes)
- Theme: Social networks, group affiliations, long-term hopes.
- Planet prompts: Social roles, idealism, friend types.

House 12 (Psychic life / Secrets / Solitude)
- Theme: Hidden patterns, spirituality, boundaries.
- Planet prompts: Hidden strengths, unconscious blocks, healing through solitude.

D. Aspects: Patterns & Major Configurations
- Identify major aspects (conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition) among personal planets and outer planets.
- For each notable aspect or configuration (T-square, Grand Trine, Stellium, Yod) include:
  - One-line description of dynamic
  - Typical life area affected (linked to houses involved)
  - Practical advice for growth and integration

E. Rulerships and House Interceptions
- Note house rulerships (what signs rule each house cusp and where those rulers fall)
- Flag intercepted signs and empty houses with conjunct rulership implications

F. Element & Mode Overview (concludes Birth Chart section)
- Elements: Fire, Earth, Air, Water — count planets & important points in each.
  - For each element: short meaning (Fire = initiative/enthusiasm; Earth = practical/stability; Air = ideas/communication; Water = feeling/intimacy).
  - If abundant (e.g., 5+ placements): Likely strengths and pitfalls (e.g., many Fire: visionary and risk-taking but may overlook details).
  - If lacking (0–1 placements): Likely developmental areas and compensatory strategies. Practical suggestions for balancing (e.g., if lacking Water, cultivate reflective practices; if lacking Earth, build routines and small achievements).
- Modes: Cardinal / Fixed / Mutable summary and what a tilt suggests for timing & adaptability.

IV. Synastry & Social Compatibility (equal emphasis on partners AND friends)
A. Overview & Method
- Explain what synastry is: overlay of two natal charts; transference dynamics vs. composite chart.
- State that this section splits attention: romantic/partner dynamics and friendship/social dynamics with equal weight.
- Recommend doing both synastry and composite for relationships that are serious.

B. Quick Compatibility Snapshot
- One-paragraph summary for immediate takeaways: primary strengths, main challenges, advice for next 6–12 months.

C. Key Areas to Check (each with partner + friend focus)
- Emotional Resonance (Moon-to-Moon, Moon aspects to Venus/Mars/Pluto, house overlays)
  - Partner: emotional attunement, security, caregiving needs.
  - Friend: emotional support style, reliability in crisis.
- Communication (Mercury to Mercury/planets, house overlays)
  - Partner: how misunderstandings arise; best communication strategies.
  - Friend: shared interests, mental stimulation, gossip vs. deep talk.
- Attraction & Affection (Venus/Mars aspects)
  - Partner: sexual and romantic chemistry, love language.
  - Friend: warmth, shared amusements, leisure compatibility.
- Long-term Potential & Commitment (Saturn, 7th house contacts, Jupiter)
  - Partner: structures, mutual responsibility, shared goals.
  - Friend: loyalty over time, pragmatic support, points where friendship matures.
- Growth & Expansion (Jupiter, 9th house overlays)
  - Partner: shared learning, travel, spiritual growth.
  - Friend: group activities, ideological support, mentorship.
- Intensity, Triggers & Healing Points (Pluto, Chiron, square/opposition patterns)
  - Partner: power struggles and therapeutic potential.
  - Friend: catalytic friendships that transform or trigger shadow material.
- Social & Group Fit (11th house overlays, Sun/Midheaven contacts)
  - Partner: how the relationship sits socially; public perception.
  - Friend: role within network, mutual contacts, shared causes.

D. House Overlays: Practical Advice
- For each house activated in the other person’s chart (e.g., their Venus in your 10th), provide template interpretations and suggested actions for partners and friends: how it shows up day-to-day, what to encourage, what to guard against.

E. Red & Green Flags
- Green flags: easy-to-apply bullet list of compatibility boosters (e.g., harmonious Moon-Venus aspects; supportive Saturn aspects).
- Red flags: recurring friction patterns and healthy boundaries/communication tactics.

V. Yearly Transit Forecast — Weekly Increments (52 weeks)
- Introduction: Explain method — focus on transits to natal planets, major planetary ingresses, retrogrades, eclipses, outer-planet aspects. Emphasize personalization: each week’s entry must reference precise natal degrees; this template assumes the analyst will calculate transit-to-natal aspects for the dates listed.

Weekly entry template (repeat for Weeks 1–52: list dates for each week)
- Week #: Date range (Week 1: 2026-04-08 → 2026-04-14; Week 2: 2026-04-15 → 2026-04-21; … Week 52: 2027-04-01 → 2027-04-07)
- Key transit highlights (list transit events to check: e.g., Sun trine natal Jupiter; Mercury retrograde begins; Saturn conjunct MC)
- Overall theme / headline (1 sentence)
- Practical effects to expect (2–4 bullets) — tailored by which natal planets are touched (analyst fills)
- Personal growth action (1 actionable suggestion)
- Relationship guidance (partner & friend equally): how to manage or enhance relationships during the week
- Career / Finance cue (1–2 bullets)
- Health & self-care tip (1 bullet)
- Days of high intensity (specific days to watch, based on exact transits)
- Affirmation/intent phrase for the week (short)

Notes on filling the weekly entries:
- For each week, compute:
  - Transit to natal conjunctions within orb (primary)
  - Squares and oppositions (challenge days)
  - Trines/sextiles (opportunities)
  - Stations (when a planet stations retrograde/direct): note the degree and natal planets within 3–5°.
  - Eclipses and lunations falling in natal houses or conjunct natal points: highlight their likely trigger topics.
  - Outer planet transits (Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) should be flagged as long-term themes that may dominate multiple adjacent weeks; give perspective on the larger arc when they appear.
- Deliver predictions in empowering, specific language tying transit type to life area (house) and natal planet: e.g., “If transiting Saturn squares your natal Sun in the 10th this week, expect responsibilities at work; prioritize long-term goals over immediate rewards.”

VI. Closing: Integration & Next Steps
- Three practical action items for the next three months based on major natal/transit patterns.
- Suggested follow-ups:
  - Deep-dive reading (e.g., progressions, solar return)
  - Couple/friend composite session if synastry flagged major work
  - Coaching prompts if many mutable stressors appear

VII. Formatting & Delivery Recommendations
- Length: 6–12 pages (approx. 2–3k words) depending on depth; weekly transit section should use the compact weekly template to remain readable.
- Tone: compassionate, practical, non-alarmist; use conditional language (“may,” “tend to,” “consider”).
- Visuals: include natal wheel image, highlight stick (top 3 planets), element chart bar, and a one-page monthly grid summarizing biggest transit events.
- Customization: swap brief examples for client-specific natal transits; always tie back to house placement for specificity.

VIII. Sample Element Balancing Guidance (to be placed at end of Birth Chart section)
- Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius)
  - Excess: impulsivity, scattered action, impatience. Balance: cultivate grounding routines, prioritize follow-through.
  - Lack: low initiative or risk-avoidant. Balance: schedule small challenges, practice public speaking or new hobbies.
- Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn)
  - Excess: rigid, slow to adapt, material over emotional. Balance: invite creative play, stretch comfort zone.
  - Lack: impractical, unreliable. Balance: adopt simple daily rituals, financial planning tools.
- Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius)
  - Excess: overthinking, detached. Balance: practice emotional check-ins, cultivate embodied practices.
  - Lack: social isolation, difficulty conceptualizing. Balance: join discussion groups, take classes.
- Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces)
  - Excess: moodiness, overwhelm. Balance: strengthen boundaries, grounding techniques.
  - Lack: emotional blindness, difficulty with intimacy. Balance: journaling, therapy, close small-circle relationships.

IX. Appendix: Quick Interpretation Cheatsheet & Report Word Counts
- Word counts per section recommendation:
  - Top Three synthesis: 100–200 words
  - Planet in sign: 75–100 words each for personal planets, outer planets 50–75
  - Planet-in-house lines: 20–40 words per planet
  - Aspects & major configurations: 75–150 words each
  - Synastry summary & red/green flags: 300–600 words
  - Weekly transits: 6–12 bullets per week (keep each week to ~100–200 words)
- Short list of language samples for positive / cautious phrasing

End of template.

Usage note: This template is intentionally modular — fill the natal placements and compute precise transit angles and dates to populate the weekly predictions. The weekly framework ensures continuous client engagement and makes the “next-year” transit forecasts actionable and easy to follow.
